name: Ransomware shuts down operations
description: Criminals lock your computers and demand payment, and your operations stop until you recover.

default: Someone opens a booby-trapped email, or an old computer never gets updates
Criminals lock every computer they can reach, backups included
You can't take orders, invoice, or run equipment
Days of lost business, plus a ransom demand
carrier: A dispatcher opens a fake invoice attachment
Ransomware locks dispatch, TMS, and billing computers
Trucks can't be dispatched and reefer loads sit at the dock
Spoiled cargo, missed delivery windows, and angry grocers
broker: Someone opens a fake rate confirmation
Ransomware locks your TMS and load records
You can't tender, track, or pay carriers
Loads miss appointments and shippers move their freight elsewhere
coldstorage: Ransomware locks inventory and temperature-monitoring computers
Product warms up with no alarm, and orders can't ship
Spoiled stock, and customers asking what else was affected

name: Fake payment request or invoice fraud
description: Someone impersonates a supplier, carrier, or your boss by email and redirects a payment to their own bank account.

default: A criminal sends an email that looks like it's from a supplier
It says their bank details have changed
Someone updates the details without calling to check
Your payment goes to the criminal and is usually gone for good
carrier: An email that looks like your fuel supplier or factoring company arrives
It says: 'our bank details changed, please update them'
Someone updates them without calling a number you already had
Your next payment, often tens of thousands, goes to criminals
broker: A 'carrier' emails new bank details just before payday
Nobody calls that carrier at a number on file
You pay the fake account, and the real carrier still wants paying
You pay twice, and the carrier stops hauling for you

name: Stolen logins to online business tools
phrase: stolen logins to your online tools
description: Someone gets into your load board, accounting, banking, or fleet portal using a stolen or guessed password.

default: A staff password is reused, leaked, or guessed
Criminals log in to your banking or supplier websites as you
They change payment details, order goods, or copy data
The losses show up weeks later
carrier: The shared load board password leaks
Criminals log in as your company
They book loads in your name or change where your payouts go
Shippers blame you, and your reputation takes the hit
broker: A TMS or load board password leaks
Criminals post fake loads or copy your carrier list
They pose as you to carriers and shippers
Stolen freight gets tied to your company name

name: Tampering with connected equipment
description: Refrigeration, grain dryers, sensors, or cameras are disrupted or accessed remotely by someone who should not be there.

default: A vendor's remote access to your equipment is left on all the time
Someone uses it to get into your equipment controls
Refrigeration, dryers, or sensors are switched off or changed
Product is ruined before anyone notices
carrier: The refrigeration vendor's remote access is always on
Someone connects to your reefer or dock controls
Temperatures change and no alarm goes off
A trailer of produce spoils before delivery
coldstorage: The refrigeration vendor's remote access is always on
Someone connects to your freezer or room controls
Setpoints change overnight with no alarm
A room of product has to be thrown away

name: A vendor or IT provider gets breached
phrase: a breach at a vendor or IT provider
description: Attackers get into your business through a company you trust, like your IT provider or an equipment vendor.

default: Your IT provider or a software vendor gets hacked
The attackers use that company's access to reach you
They move around quietly for weeks
Ransomware or data theft that started somewhere else
carrier: Your TMS, ELD, or IT provider is breached
Attackers use its connection into your office
Dispatch and customer data is exposed
You're shut down, and you weren't even the target

name: Losing data you cannot get back
phrase: losing data you cannot get back
description: Files, records, or accounting data are destroyed and there is no way to restore them.

default: A computer dies, is stolen, or gets locked by ransomware
There's no backup that actually works
Invoices, records, and customer lists are gone
Weeks of rebuilding, and some of it never comes back
carrier: The office computer with dispatch records and rate sheets dies
The only backup is an old USB drive
BOLs, proof of delivery, and invoices are gone
You can't bill for loads you already delivered

name: Misuse of shared or leftover accounts
phrase: misuse of shared or leftover accounts
description: Shared logins or ex-employee accounts are used without anyone knowing who did it.

default: Several people share one login, or an ex-employee's account still works
Someone misuses it
The records can't show who did what
You can't prove what happened, or lock out just that person
carrier: Dispatchers share one login, and a driver who left still knows it
Someone books or changes loads with it
The logs just say 'dispatch'
You can't tell who did it, or lock out just them

name: Load redirected to thieves
phrase: a load being redirected to thieves
description: Someone posing as your broker or customer asks for a new pickup or delivery address, one person changes it, and the load goes to thieves.

default: Criminals get into a staff email account, or fake a customer's email
They see which shipments are worth the most
They ask for a 'new delivery address', and one person changes it
The load goes to thieves
carrier: A dispatcher's email password is phished
Criminals read your shipment history and pick a high-value reefer load
Posing as the broker, they email a 'new delivery address'
One dispatcher changes it alone, and the load is gone
broker: Criminals phish your email or fake a shipper's
They pick a high-value load from your email threads
They send the carrier a 'revised' delivery address
The carrier delivers to thieves, and you get the blame
